questions.question: What should you do before writing any code for a custom ASM tool?
options: Buy a domain name for the project
Identify the gap in existing tools and design the solution and implementation approach
Write the press release
Choose a logo
questions.explanation: Tool development starts with gap analysis: what do Amass, httpx, nuclei, and friends not do that you need? Design against a real gap before implementing.

questions.question: Which is a security best practice when developing reconnaissance tooling?
options: Hardcoding API credentials for convenience
Validating inputs, handling secrets safely, and building in rate limiting and safe defaults
Disabling TLS verification to avoid certificate errors
Running everything as root
questions.explanation: Security tools must themselves be secure and respectful: validate untrusted input, keep credentials out of code, default to conservative scanning behavior.

questions.question: Why is documentation critical for a custom tool you plan to open source?
options: GitHub requires a README before you can push
Without clear docs on installation, usage, and scope of use, others cannot adopt or contribute to the tool
Documentation improves runtime performance
It is only needed for commercial products
questions.explanation: Adoption and contribution are what make open source work. Clear installation steps, usage examples, and ethical-use guidance are what turn working code into a usable community tool.

questions.question: What belongs in the testing phase before releasing a custom ASM tool?
options: Performance testing, security review, and gathering community feedback
Only checking that it compiles
Testing exclusively against production targets you don't own
Skipping tests since recon tools are read-only
questions.explanation: Before release: verify performance under realistic load, review the tool's own security posture, and get feedback — bugs in recon tools can harm targets or produce misleading results.

questions.question: When you improve an existing open-source ASM tool, what is generally the best path?
options: Keep the improvement private to maintain an advantage
Contribute the change upstream so the whole community benefits and you don't maintain a permanent fork
Republish the whole tool under your own name
Sell the patch to the maintainers
questions.explanation: Contributing upstream shares the benefit, gets your code reviewed by maintainers, and avoids the long-term cost of maintaining a divergent fork.
